sentences.en: I'm going to talk to you about some stuff that's in this book of mine that I hope will resonate with other things you've already heard, and I'll try to make some connections myself, in case you miss them.
sentences.zh: 我要跟你谈谈我这本书中的一些东西 我希望它们能与你已经听到的其他事物产生共鸣, 我会自己做一些联系,以防你想念它们。

sentences.en: But I want to start with what I call the "official dogma."
sentences.zh: 但我想从我所谓的"官方教条"开始

sentences.en: The official dogma of what? The official dogma of all Western industrial societies.
sentences.zh: 官方的教条是什么?

sentences.en: And the official dogma runs like this: if we are interested in maximizing the welfare of our citizens, the way to do that is to maximize individual freedom.
sentences.zh: 官方的教条是这样运行的: 如果我们对最大限度地提高我们公民的福利感兴趣, 这样做的方法就是最大限度地提高个人自由。

sentences.en: The reason for this is both that freedom is, in and of itself, good, valuable, worthwhile, essential to being human, and because if people have freedom, then each of us can act on our own
sentences.zh: 这是因为自由本身是善良的,有价值的,值得的,是人类不可或缺的 因为如果人们有自由,那么我们每个人都可以自己行动

sentences.en: to do the things that will maximize our welfare, and no one has to decide on our behalf.
sentences.zh: 来做能让福利最大化的事 没有人能代表我们做决定

sentences.en: The way to maximize freedom is to maximize choice.
sentences.zh: 尽量扩大自由的方式是尽量扩大选择。

sentences.en: The more choice people have, the more freedom they have, and the more freedom they have, the more welfare they have.
sentences.zh: 人们的选择越多,他们就越有自由,他们就越有自由,他们就越有福利。

sentences.en: This, I think, is so deeply embedded in the water supply that it wouldn't occur to anyone to question it.
sentences.zh: 我认为,这深深植根于水供应中 以至于没有人会质疑它

sentences.en: And it's also deeply embedded in our lives.
sentences.zh: 它也深深植根于我们的生活。

sentences.en: I'll give you some examples of what modern progress has made possible for us.
sentences.zh: 我举几个例子来说明 现代的进步使我们得以实现。

sentences.en: This is my supermarket. Not such a big one.
sentences.zh: 这是我的超市 没那么大

sentences.en: I want to say just a word about salad dressing.
sentences.zh: 我想说说沙拉酱的事

sentences.en: A hundred seventy-five salad dressings in my supermarket, if you don't count the 10 extra-virgin olive oils and 12 balsamic vinegars you could buy to make a very large number of your own salad dressings, in the off-chance that none of the 175 the store has on offer suit you.
sentences.zh: 在我的超市里有一百七十五个沙拉酱, 如果你不计10种额外的橄榄油 和12种白葡萄酒, 你可以买来做很多你自己的沙拉酱,

sentences.en: So this is what the supermarket is like.
sentences.zh: 超市就是这样的

sentences.en: And then you go to the consumer electronics store to set up a stereo system -- speakers, CD player, tape player, tuner, amplifier -- and in this one single consumer electronics store, there are that many stereo systems.
sentences.zh: 然后你去消费电子商店 建立一个音响系统-- 扬声器,CD播放器,磁带播放器,调音器,放大器-- 在这个单一的消费电子商店里, 有很多音响系统。

sentences.en: We can construct six and a half million different stereo systems out of the components that are on offer in one store.
sentences.zh: 我们可以建造650万个不同的立体系统 从一个商店里提供的部件中

sentences.en: You've got to admit that's a lot of choice.
sentences.zh: 你得承认这是个很大的选择

sentences.en: In other domains -- the world of communications.
sentences.zh: 在其他领域 -- -- 通信界。

sentences.en: There was a time, when I was a boy, when you could get any kind of telephone service you wanted, as long as it came from Ma Bell.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间,当我还是个孩子, 你可以得到任何类型的电话服务 你想要的, 只要它来自玛贝尔。

sentences.en: You rented your phone, you didn't buy it.
sentences.zh: 你租了手机,没买

sentences.en: One consequence of that, by the way, is that the phone never broke.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句,一个后果是 电话从不坏

sentences.en: And those days are gone. We now have an almost unlimited variety of phones, especially in the world of cell phones.
sentences.zh: 而那些日子已经过去了。我们现在拥有的电话种类几乎是无限的, 特别是在手机的世界。

sentences.en: These are cell phones of the future. My favorite is the middle one -- the MP3 player, nose hair trimmer, and crème brûlée torch.
sentences.zh: 这些是未来的手机。我最喜欢的是中间的——MP3播放器、鼻毛剪发机和Crème Brlée火炬。

sentences.en: And if -- (Laughter) if by some chance you haven't seen that in your store yet, you can rest assured that one day soon, you will.
sentences.zh: 如果... (笑声) 如果你在你的店里还没有看到这一点, 你可以放心,很快有一天,你会的。

sentences.en: And what this does is it leads people to walk into their stores, asking this question.
sentences.zh: 这导致人们走进他们的商店 问这个问题。

sentences.en: And do you know what the answer to this question now is?
sentences.zh: 你知道现在这个问题的答案是什么吗?

sentences.en: The answer is "no." It is not possible to buy a cell phone that doesn't do too much.
sentences.zh: 答案是"不" 不可能买一个不会做太多的手机

sentences.en: So, in other aspects of life that are much more significant than buying things, the same explosion of choice is true.
sentences.zh: 所以,在生活的其他方面 比买东西更重要, 同样的选择爆炸是真实的。

sentences.en: Health care. It is no longer the case in the United States that you go to the doctor, and the doctor tells you what to do.
sentences.zh: 医疗保健。在美国,你不再去看医生,医生告诉你该怎么做。

sentences.en: Instead, you go to the doctor, and the doctor tells you, "Well, we could do A, or we could do B.
sentences.zh: 相反,你去看医生, 医生告诉你,“嗯,我们可以做A,或者我们可以做B。

sentences.en: A has these benefits and these risks. B has these benefits and these risks.
sentences.zh: A有这些好处和风险。B有这些好处和风险。

sentences.en: What do you want to do?" And you say, "Doc, what should I do?"
sentences.zh: 你想做什么? 你说,"医生,我该怎么办?"

sentences.en: And the doc says, "A has these benefits and risks, and B has these benefits and risks.
sentences.zh: 医生说,“A有这些好处和风险,B有这些好处和风险。

sentences.en: What do you want to do?" And you say, "If you were me, Doc, what would you do?"
sentences.zh: 你想做什么?" 你说,"如果你是我,医生,你会怎么做?"

sentences.en: And the doc says, "But I'm not you." And the result is -- we call it "patient autonomy," which makes it sound like a good thing, but what it really is a shifting of the burden and the responsibility for decision-making
sentences.zh: 医生说,“但我不是你。”结果就是,我们称之为“病人自主”, 这使得这听起来像一件好事, 但它实际上是一个负担的转移和决策的责任。

sentences.en: from somebody who knows something -- namely, the doctor -- to somebody who knows nothing and is almost certainly sick and thus, not in the best shape to be making decisions -- namely, the patient.
sentences.zh: (笑声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声(掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声(掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声)。

sentences.en: There's enormous marketing of prescription drugs to people like you and me, which, if you think about it, makes no sense at all, since we can't buy them.
sentences.zh: 有巨大的营销处方药 向像你我这样的人, 如果你考虑一下, 没有任何意义, 因为我们不能买他们。

sentences.en: Why do they market to us if we can't buy them?
sentences.zh: 如果我们买不到,为什么他们要卖给我们?

sentences.en: The answer is that they expect us to call our doctors the next morning and ask for our prescriptions to be changed.
sentences.zh: 答案是,他们希望我们第二天早上打电话给我们的医生,要求改变我们的处方。

sentences.en: Something as dramatic as our identity has now become a matter of choice, as this slide is meant to indicate.
sentences.zh: 和我们的身份一样戏剧性的东西 现在已经成为一个选择的问题, 正如这张幻灯片的意思是表明。

sentences.en: We don't inherit an identity; we get to invent it.
sentences.zh: 我们不继承一个身份,我们可以发明它。

sentences.en: And we get to reinvent ourselves as often as we like.
sentences.zh: 我们能想怎样就怎样重塑自己

sentences.en: And that means that every day, when you wake up in the morning, you have to decide what kind of person you want to be.
sentences.zh: 这意味着,每天,当你早上醒来时, 你必须决定你想成为什么样的人。

sentences.en: With respect to marriage and family: there was a time when the default assumption that almost everyone had is that you got married as soon as you could, and then you started having kids as soon as you could.
sentences.zh: 关于婚姻和家庭:有一段时间, 几乎每个人都有默认的假设 即你尽快结婚, 然后,你开始 尽快有孩子。

sentences.en: The only real choice was who, not when, and not what you did after.
sentences.zh: 唯一真正的选择是 谁,不是什么时候, 而不是你做了什么之后。

sentences.en: Nowadays, everything is very much up for grabs.
sentences.zh: 现在,一切都要被抢了。

sentences.en: I teach wonderfully intelligent students, and I assign 20 percent less work than I used to.
sentences.zh: 我教过聪明的学生, 我分配的工作比以前少20%。

sentences.en: And it's not because they're less smart, and it's not because they're less diligent.
sentences.zh: 也不是因为他们不够聪明 也不是因为他们不够勤奋

sentences.en: It's because they are preoccupied, asking themselves, "Should I get married or not? Should I get married now?
sentences.zh: 因为他们心烦意乱 问自己 "我该不该结婚?

sentences.en: Should I get married later? Should I have kids first or a career first?"
sentences.zh: 我该晚点结婚 还是先生孩子?

sentences.en: All of these are consuming questions. And they're going to answer these questions, whether or not it means not doing all the work I assign and not getting a good grade in my courses.
sentences.zh: 所有这些问题都在消磨。他们要回答这些问题, 是否意味着不做我指派的所有工作, 并且没有在我的课程中获得一个好的成绩。

sentences.en: And indeed they should. These are important questions to answer.
sentences.zh: 他们确实应该回答,这些都是需要回答的重要问题。

sentences.en: Work. We are blessed, as Carl was pointing out, with the technology that enables us to work every minute of every day from any place on the planet -- except the Randolph Hotel.
sentences.zh: 工作。正如卡尔所指出的,我们很幸运, 有了这种技术,我们每天每分钟 都能从地球上的任何地方工作, 除了兰道夫酒店。

sentences.en: (Laughter) (Applause) There is one corner, by the way, that I'm not going to tell anybody about, where the WiFi actually works.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句,有一个角落, 我不会告诉任何人, WiFi 实际上在哪里工作。

sentences.en: I'm not telling you about it, because I want to use it.
sentences.zh: 我不会告诉你的 因为我想用它

sentences.en: So what this means, this incredible freedom of choice we have with respect to work, is that we have to make a decision, again and again and again, about whether we should or shouldn't be working.
sentences.zh: 所以,这意味着,这个令人难以置信的选择自由 我们的工作, 是我们必须做出一个决定, 一次又一次地, 我们是否应该工作。

sentences.en: We can go to watch our kid play soccer, and we have our cell phone on one hip and our Blackberry on our other hip, and our laptop, presumably, on our laps.
sentences.zh: 我们可以去看我们的孩子踢足球, 我们的手机在一个臀部, 我们的黑莓在我们的另一个臀部, 和我们的笔记本电脑,大概,在我们腿上。

sentences.en: And even if they're all shut off, every minute that we're watching our kid mutilate a soccer game, we are also asking ourselves, "Should I answer this cell phone call?
sentences.zh: 即使他们全部关闭, 每一分钟 我们看着我们的孩子 肢解一个足球比赛, 我们也在问自己, "我应该接这个电话吗?

sentences.en: Should I respond to this email? Should I draft this letter?"
sentences.zh: 我该对这封邮件作出回应吗?我该起草这封信吗?”

sentences.en: And even if the answer to the question is "no," it's certainly going to make the experience of your kid's soccer game very different than it would've been.
sentences.zh: 即使问题的答案是"不" 肯定会让你孩子的足球赛经历 变得完全不同

sentences.en: So everywhere we look, big things and small things, material things and lifestyle things, life is a matter of choice.
sentences.zh: 因此,我们到处看,大的东西和小的东西, 物质的东西和生活方式的东西, 生活是一个选择的问题。

sentences.en: And the world we used to live in looked like this.
sentences.zh: 而我们曾经生活在这样的世界里。

sentences.en: [Well, actually, they are written in stone.]
sentences.zh: [实际上,它们是用石头写的。 ]

sentences.en: That is to say, there were some choices, but not everything was a matter of choice.
sentences.zh: 也就是说,有一些选择,但并非一切都是选择的问题。

sentences.en: The world we now live in looks like this.
sentences.zh: 我们现在生活的世界是这样的。

sentences.en: [The Ten Commandments Do-It-Yourself Kit] And the question is: Is this good news or bad news?
sentences.zh: 问题是:这是好消息还是坏消息?

sentences.en: And the answer is "yes." (Laughter) We all know what's good about it, so I'm going to talk about what's bad about it.
sentences.zh: 答案是:"是的。" (笑声)我们都知道什么是好的, 所以我要谈谈什么是坏的。

sentences.en: All of this choice has two effects, two negative effects on people.
sentences.zh: 所有这些选择都对人有两种影响,两种负面影响。

sentences.en: One effect, paradoxically, is that it produces paralysis rather than liberation.
sentences.zh: 矛盾的是,一种影响是,它造成瘫痪,而不是解放。

sentences.en: With so many options to choose from, people find it very difficult to choose at all.
sentences.zh: 有了这么多的选择,人们发现很难选择。

sentences.en: I'll give you one very dramatic example of this, a study that was done of investments in voluntary retirement plans.
sentences.zh: 我给你一个非常戏剧化的例子, 一项对自愿退休计划投资的研究。

sentences.en: A colleague of mine got access to investment records from Vanguard, the gigantic mutual fund company, of about a million employees and about 2,000 different workplaces.
sentences.zh: 我的一个同事从一个巨大的共同基金公司先锋公司获得了投资记录,该公司约有100万雇员和大约2 000个不同的工作场所。

sentences.en: What she found is that for every 10 mutual funds the employer offered, rate of participation went down two percent.
sentences.zh: 她发现,每10个共同基金雇主提供,参与率下降2%。

sentences.en: You offer 50 funds -- 10 percent fewer employees participate than if you only offer five.
sentences.zh: 你提供50个基金 -- 雇员的参与比只提供5个少10%。

sentences.en: Why? Because with 50 funds to choose from, it's so damn hard to decide which fund to choose, that you'll just put it off till tomorrow, and then tomorrow and then tomorrow and tomorrow,
sentences.zh: 为什么？因为有 50 只基金可供选择，很难决定选择哪只基金，所以你只能推迟到明天，然后明天，然后明天和明天，

sentences.en: and, of course, tomorrow never comes. Understand that not only does this mean that people are going to have to eat dog food when they retire because they don't have enough money put away, it also means that making the decision is so hard
sentences.zh: 当然，明天永远不会到来。要明白，这不仅意味着人们在退休时将不得不吃狗粮，因为他们没有足够的钱存起来，而且还意味着做出决定是如此困难

sentences.en: that they pass up significant matching money from the employer.
sentences.zh: 他们放弃了雇主提供的大量匹配资金。

sentences.en: By not participating, they are passing up as much as 5,000 dollars a year from the employer, who would happily match their contribution.
sentences.zh: 如果不参与，他们每年就会从雇主那里损失多达 5,000 美元，而雇主很乐意与他们的捐款相匹配。

sentences.en: So paralysis is a consequence of having too many choices.
sentences.zh: 因此，瘫痪是选择太多的结果。

sentences.en: And I think it makes the world look like this.
sentences.zh: 我认为这让世界看起来像这样。

sentences.en: [And lastly, for all eternity, French, bleu cheese or ranch?]
sentences.zh: [最后，永远，法式、蓝纹奶酪还是牧场？]

sentences.en: (Laughter) You really want to get the decision right if it's for all eternity, right?
sentences.zh: （笑声）如果这个决定是永恒的，你真的很想做出正确的决定，对吧？

sentences.en: You don't want to pick the wrong mutual fund or wrong salad dressing.
sentences.zh: 您不想选择错误的共同基金或错误的沙拉酱。

sentences.en: So that's one effect. The second effect is that, even if we manage to overcome the paralysis and make a choice, we end up less satisfied with the result of the choice than we would be if we had fewer options to choose from.
sentences.zh: 这就是效果之一。第二个影响是，即使我们设法克服瘫痪并做出选择，我们最终对选择结果的满意度也会低于我们可供选择的选项较少时的满意度。

sentences.en: And there are several reasons for this. One of them is, with a lot of different salad dressings to choose from, if you buy one and it's not perfect -- and what salad dressing is? -- it's easy to imagine that you could've made a different choice
sentences.zh: 这有几个原因。其中之一是，有很多不同的沙拉酱可供选择，如果你买了一种但它并不完美——那么什么是沙拉酱呢？ ——很容易想象你可以做出不同的选择

sentences.en: that would've been better. And what happens is, this imagined alternative induces you to regret the decision you made, and this regret subtracts from the satisfaction you get out of the decision you made,
sentences.zh: 那会更好。发生的情况是，这种想象中的选择会让你后悔自己所做的决定，而这种后悔会降低你从所做决定中获得的满足感，

sentences.en: even if it was a good decision. The more options there are, the easier it is to regret anything at all that is disappointing about the option that you chose.
sentences.zh: 即使这是一个好的决定。选择越多，你就越容易对你所选择的选项感到失望的事情感到后悔。

sentences.en: Second, what economists call "opportunity costs."
sentences.zh: 其次，经济学家所说的“机会成本”。

sentences.en: Dan Gilbert made a big point this morning of talking about how much the way in which we value things depends on what we compare them to.
sentences.zh: 丹·吉尔伯特今天早上提出了一个重要观点，即我们评价事物的方式在多大程度上取决于我们将它们与什么进行比较。

sentences.en: Well, when there are lots of alternatives to consider, it's easy to imagine the attractive features of alternatives that you reject that make you less satisfied with the alternative that you've chosen.
sentences.zh: 好吧，当有很多替代方案需要考虑时，很容易想象您拒绝的替代方案的有吸引力的功能，这些功能会让您对您所选择的替代方案不太满意。

sentences.en: Here's an example. [I can't stop thinking about those other available parking spaces on W 85th Street] If you're not a New Yorker, I apologize.
sentences.zh: 这是一个例子。 [我无法停止思考西 85 街的其他可用停车位] 如果您不是纽约人，我深表歉意。

sentences.en: Here's what you're supposed to be thinking.
sentences.zh: 这就是你应该想到的。

sentences.en: Here's this couple on the Hamptons. Very expensive real estate.
sentences.zh: 这是汉普顿的这对夫妇。非常昂贵的房地产。

sentences.en: Gorgeous beach. Beautiful day. They have it all to themselves.
sentences.zh: 美丽的海滩。美好的一天。他们拥有一切。

sentences.en: What could be better? "Damn it," this guy is thinking, "It's August. Everybody in my Manhattan neighborhood is away.
sentences.zh: 还有什么更好的呢？ “该死的，”这家伙心里想，“现在是八月。我曼哈顿社区的每个人都不在了。

sentences.en: I could be parking right in front of my building."
sentences.zh: 我可以把车停在我的大楼前。”

sentences.en: And he spends two weeks nagged by the idea that he is missing the opportunity, day after day, to have a great parking space.
sentences.zh: 他花了两周时间担心自己日复一日地错过了拥有一个很棒的停车位的机会。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Opportunity costs subtract from the satisfaction that we get out of what we choose, even when what we choose is terrific.
sentences.zh: （笑声）机会成本会减去我们从选择中获得的满足感，即使我们选择的东西非常棒。

sentences.en: And the more options there are to consider, the more attractive features of these options are going to be reflected by us as opportunity costs.
sentences.zh: 需要考虑的选择越多，这些选择的更具吸引力的特征就会被我们反映为机会成本。

sentences.en: Here's another example. (Laughter) Now, this cartoon makes a lot of points.
sentences.zh: 下面是另一个例子。 (笑声)现在,这卡通 做了很多要点。

sentences.en: It makes points about living in the moment as well, and probably about doing things slowly.
sentences.zh: 它也说明了生活的时刻, 以及可能关于做事情的缓慢。

sentences.en: But one point it makes is that whenever you're choosing one thing, you're choosing not to do other things, and those other things may have lots of attractive features, and it's going to make what you're doing less attractive.
sentences.zh: 但有一点是,当你选择一件事时, 你选择不做其他的事情, 而那些其他的事情可能有很多 吸引人的特征,

sentences.en: Third: escalation of expectations. This hit me when I went to replace my jeans.
sentences.zh: 第三:期望的上升。当我去换牛仔裤的时候,我被打中了。

sentences.en: I wear jeans almost all the time. There was a time when jeans came in one flavor, and you bought them, and they fit like crap.
sentences.zh: 我几乎总是穿牛仔裤。有一次牛仔裤 以一种口味,你买了它们,它们就像垃圾一样。

sentences.en: They were incredibly uncomfortable, and if you wore them long enough and washed them enough times, they started to feel OK.
sentences.zh: 他们非常不舒服 如果你穿得够久 洗得够久 他们开始感觉很好

sentences.en: I went to replace my jeans after years of wearing these old ones.
sentences.zh: 穿了这么多年的旧牛仔裤后 我去换了牛仔裤

sentences.en: I said, "I want a pair of jeans. Here's my size."
sentences.zh: 我说:"我要一条牛仔裤,这是我的尺寸"

sentences.en: And the shopkeeper said, "Do you want slim fit, easy fit, relaxed fit?
sentences.zh: 店主说:"你想要瘦的, 轻而易举的,轻而易举的吗?

sentences.en: You want button fly or zipper fly? You want stonewashed or acid-washed?
sentences.zh: 你想要按键飞还是拉链飞?

sentences.en: Do you want them distressed? Do you want boot cut, tapered?" Blah, blah, blah on and on he went.
sentences.zh: 你想让他们受苦吗?

sentences.en: My jaw dropped. And after I recovered, I said, "I want the kind that used to be the only kind."
sentences.zh: 我的下巴掉下来,我恢复后,我说, “我希望那种曾经是唯一的那种。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) He had no idea what that was.
sentences.zh: (笑声) 他不知道那是什么。

sentences.en: (Laughter) So I spent an hour trying on all these damn jeans, and I walked out of the store -- truth -- with the best-fitting jeans I had ever had.
sentences.zh: (笑声) 所以我花了一个小时 尝试所有这些该死的牛仔裤, 我走出了商店-- 说实话-- 和最好的牛仔裤 我曾经有过。

sentences.en: I did better. All this choice made it possible for me to do better.
sentences.zh: 我做得更好 所有的这些选择 都使我得以做得更好

sentences.en: But -- I felt worse. Why? I wrote a whole book to try to explain this to myself.
sentences.zh: 但我感觉更糟 为什么 我写了一整本书来解释

sentences.en: The reason is -- (Laughter) The reason I felt worse is that with all of these options available, my expectations about how good a pair of jeans should be went up.
sentences.zh: 原因是--(笑声)我感到更糟糕的原因是,有了所有这些选择,我对一条牛仔裤应该有多好的期望应该提高。

sentences.en: I had very low, no particular expectations when they only came in one flavor.
sentences.zh: 我非常低,没有特别的期望 当它们只有一个味道。

sentences.en: When they came in 100 flavors, damn it, one of them should've been perfect.
sentences.zh: 当他们以100的口味, 该死的,他们中的一个 应该已经完美。

sentences.en: And what I got was good, but it wasn't perfect.
sentences.zh: 我得到的东西是好的, 但它不是完美的。

sentences.en: And so I compared what I got to what I expected, and what I got was disappointing in comparison to what I expected.
sentences.zh: 所以我比较我得到的 与我所期望的, 和我所期望的相比,我得到的 令人失望。

sentences.en: Adding options to people's lives can't help but increase the expectations people have about how good those options will be.
sentences.zh: 给人们的生活增加选择 只会增加人们对于这些选择有多好的期待

sentences.en: And what that's going to produce is less satisfaction with results, even when they're good results.
sentences.zh: 其结果是,即使结果良好,对结果的满意度也较低。

sentences.en: [It all looks so great. I can't wait to be disappointed.]
sentences.zh: [看起来太棒了,我迫不及待要失望]

sentences.en: Nobody in the world of marketing knows this.
sentences.zh: 营销界没有人知道这一点。

sentences.en: Because if they did, you wouldn't all know what this was about.
sentences.zh: 因为如果他们这么做了,你们不会都知道这是怎么回事

sentences.en: The truth is more like this. [Everything was better back when everything was worse.]
sentences.zh: 事实更是这样。 [一切都好,当一切都变糟了。 ]

sentences.en: The reason that everything was better back when everything was worse is that when everything was worse, it was actually possible for people to have experiences that were a pleasant surprise.
sentences.zh: 当一切变得更糟时 一切都会好起来的原因是 当每件事都变得更糟时 人们实际上有可能 体验到一个令人愉快的惊喜

sentences.en: Nowadays, the world we live in -- we affluent, industrialized citizens, with perfection the expectation -- the best you can ever hope for is that stuff is as good as you expect it to be.
sentences.zh: 现在,我们所生活的世界 -- -- 我们富有、工业化的公民, 满怀期望 -- -- 你所希望的最好的就是 东西和你所期望的一样好。

sentences.en: You will never be pleasantly surprised, because your expectations, my expectations, have gone through the roof.
sentences.zh: 你永远也不会感到惊讶,因为你的期望,我的期望,已经到了顶峰。

sentences.en: The secret to happiness -- this is what you all came for -- the secret to happiness is: low expectations.
sentences.zh: 幸福的秘密 -- -- 这就是你们来的目的 -- -- 幸福的秘密是:低期望。

sentences.en: (Laughter) [You'll do] (Applause) (Laughter) I want to say -- just a little autobiographical moment --
sentences.zh: (笑声) [你会做] (掌声)(笑声) 我想说-- 只是一个自传片刻--

sentences.en: that I actually am married to a wife, and she's really quite wonderful.
sentences.zh: 我娶了个老婆 她真的很棒

sentences.en: I couldn't have done better. I didn't settle.
sentences.zh: 我不能做得更好,我还没定下来

sentences.en: But settling isn't always such a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 但安顿并不总是一件坏事。

sentences.en: Finally, one consequence of buying a bad-fitting pair of jeans when there is only one kind to buy is that when you are dissatisfied and you ask why, who's responsible, the answer is clear: the world is responsible.
sentences.zh: 最后,买一对不合适的牛仔裤,只有一种可以买,其后果是当你不满意,问为什么,谁负责,答案是清楚的:世界是负责任的。

sentences.en: What could you do? When there are hundreds of different styles of jeans available and you buy one that is disappointing and you ask why, who's responsible, it is equally clear that the answer to the question is "you."
sentences.zh: 你能做什么?当有数百种不同的牛仔裤 你买了一个令人失望的牛仔裤 你问为什么,谁负责, 这个问题的答案是“你”同样清楚。

sentences.en: You could have done better. With a hundred different kinds of jeans on display, there is no excuse for failure.
sentences.zh: 你本可以做得更好 有了百种不同的牛仔裤 就没有失败的借口

sentences.en: And so when people make decisions, and even though the results of the decisions are good, they feel disappointed about them; they blame themselves.
sentences.zh: 因此,当人们作出决定时,即使这些决定的结果是好的,但他们对此感到失望;他们责备自己。

sentences.en: Clinical depression has exploded in the industrial world in the last generation.
sentences.zh: 临床抑郁症在上一代的工业世界爆发。

sentences.en: I believe a significant -- not the only, but a significant -- contributor to this explosion of depression and also suicide, is that people have experiences that are disappointing because their standards are so high, and then when they have to explain these experiences to themselves,
sentences.zh: 我认为,造成这种抑郁症和自杀现象的一个重要因素,不是唯一因素,而是一个重要的因素,就是人们的经历令人失望,因为他们的标准太高,然后当他们不得不向自己解释这些经历时,

sentences.en: they think they're at fault. So the net result is that we do better in general, objectively, and we feel worse.
sentences.zh: 最终结果是我们做得更好 客观 并且我们感到更糟糕

sentences.en: So let me remind you: this is the official dogma, the one that we all take to be true, and it's all false.
sentences.zh: 让我提醒你,这是正式的教条, 我们都认为是真实的, 这一切都是假的。

sentences.en: It is not true. There's no question that some choice is better than none.
sentences.zh: 这不是真的,毫无疑问,有些选择胜于任何选择

sentences.en: But it doesn't follow from that more choice is better than some choice.
sentences.zh: 但它并没有从更多的选择 胜过一些选择。

sentences.en: There's some magical amount. I don't know what it is.
sentences.zh: 有一些神奇的数字 我不知道是什么

sentences.en: I'm pretty confident that we have long since passed the point where options improve our welfare.
sentences.zh: 我很有信心 我们早就过了选择改善我们福利的关头

sentences.en: Now, as a policy matter -- I'm almost done -- as a policy matter, the thing to think about is this: what enables all of this choice in industrial societies is material affluence.
sentences.zh: 现在,作为一个政策事项 -- 我几乎完成了 -- 作为一个政策事项, 需要考虑的是: 工业社会的所有选择都是物质财富。

sentences.en: There are lots of places in the world, and we have heard about several of them, where their problem is not that they have too much choice.
sentences.zh: 世界上有许多地方,我们听说过其中一些地方,在那里,他们的问题不是他们有太多的选择。

sentences.en: Their problem is they have too little. So the stuff I'm talking about is the peculiar problem of modern, affluent, Western societies.
sentences.zh: 他们的问题是他们太少了。所以我说的是 现代,富裕,西方社会的特殊问题。

sentences.en: And what is so frustrating and infuriating is this: Steve Levitt talked to you yesterday about how these expensive and difficult-to-install child seats don't help.
sentences.zh: 令人如此沮丧和愤怒的是：史蒂夫莱维特昨天与您谈论了这些昂贵且难以安装的儿童座椅如何无济于事。

sentences.en: It's a waste of money. What I'm telling you is that these expensive, complicated choices -- it's not simply that they don't help.
sentences.zh: 这是浪费钱。我要告诉你的是，这些昂贵、复杂的选择——不仅仅是因为它们没有帮助。

sentences.en: They actually hurt. They actually make us worse off.
sentences.zh: 他们确实受伤了。它们实际上让我们的境况变得更糟。

sentences.en: If some of what enables people in our societies to make all of the choices we make were shifted to societies in which people have too few options, not only would those people's lives be improved,
sentences.zh: 如果我们社会中的人们能够做出我们所做的所有选择的某些因素转移到人们选择太少的社会中，那么不仅这些人的生活会得到改善，

sentences.en: but ours would be improved also. This is what economists call a "Pareto-improving move."
sentences.zh: 但我们的也会得到改善。这就是经济学家所说的“帕累托改进举措”。

sentences.en: Income redistribution will make everyone better off, not just poor people, because of how all this excess choice plagues us.
sentences.zh: 收入再分配将使每个人都过得更好，而不仅仅是穷人，因为所有这些过多的选择如何困扰着我们。

sentences.en: So to conclude. [You can be anything you want to be -- no limits.]
sentences.zh: 所以得出结论。 [你可以成为任何你想成为的人——没有限制。]

sentences.en: You're supposed to read this cartoon and, being a sophisticated person, say, "Ah! What does this fish know? Nothing is possible in this fishbowl."
sentences.zh: 作为一个老练的人，你应该读这幅漫画并说：“啊！这条鱼知道什么？在这个鱼缸里什么都不可能发生。”

sentences.en: Impoverished imagination, a myopic view of the world -- that's the way I read it at first.
sentences.zh: 贫乏的想象力，短视的世界观——这就是我一开始读这本书的方式。

sentences.en: The more I thought about it, however, the more I came to the view that this fish knows something.
sentences.zh: 然而，我越想越觉得这条鱼懂得一些东西。

sentences.en: Because the truth of the matter is, if you shatter the fishbowl so that everything is possible, you don't have freedom.
sentences.zh: 因为事情的真相是，如果你打碎鱼缸，让一切皆有可能，你就没有自由。

sentences.en: You have paralysis. If you shatter this fishbowl so that everything is possible, you decrease satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 你患有瘫痪。如果你打碎这个鱼缸，让一切皆有可能，那么你的满意度就会降低。

sentences.en: You increase paralysis, and you decrease satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 你会增加麻痹感，也会降低满意度。

sentences.en: Everybody needs a fishbowl. This one is almost certainly too limited -- perhaps even for the fish, certainly for us.
sentences.zh: 每个人都需要一个鱼缸。几乎可以肯定，这一点太有限了——甚至可能对鱼来说，当然对我们来说也是如此。

sentences.en: But the absence of some metaphorical fishbowl is a recipe for misery and, I suspect, disaster.
sentences.zh: 但缺乏某种隐喻性的鱼缸会导致痛苦，我怀疑还会导致灾难。

sentences.en: Thank you very much. (Applause)
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。 （掌声）
